Parameters: (1) surface geometry — width sufficient for a full folio (typically 40-45 cm), adjustable tilt from near-horizontal to steep; (2) support — a post (fixed, telescoping, or articulated) on a stable base; (3) page-holding mechanism — a clip, bar, or weighted edge that keeps pages from lifting under performer movement or air; (4) mounting class — floor, desk, or wall. Persistence mechanism: manufactured in bulk from wood, MDF, aluminum, or plastic, distributed through retail and music-store channels, maintained through consumer ownership cycles; the form persists as a product category via continuous production, design iteration, and replacement. payload.body: Sheet music is a human-made document bearing a musical score in standard notation: a page or set of pages whose printed, engraved, or digitally rendered marks — staves, notes, clefs, dynamic and articulation marks, and text — encode a musical work, laid out for a human reader at performance distance. Parameters: (1) notation system — the marks follow the shared syntactic rules of musical notation (staves, clefs, note values, dynamics), without which the page is uninterpretable; (2) part vs. full-score layout — a single instrument or voice part or a complete reduction, with system layout and page turns arranged for a performing reader; (3) format — printed or engraved paper of standard sizes (letter, A4, full-score folio) or a paginated digital rendering of the same layout; (4) reading geometry — orientation, margins, and sizing chosen so a performer can read ahead while playing. Persistence mechanism: produced by typesetting, engraving, printing, or digital typesetting; distributed through music publishers, retail, and licensing; maintained through reprints and successive editions; the form persists as a product category, the designed held-object of the music stand. [formal: folium musicum | substrate: matter | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: A staff (stave) is a notational structure of parallel horizontal lines — standardly five, with the four spaces between them — whose successive lines and spaces encode successive steps of a diatonic scale, forming the reference frame in which written pitches are placed. Parameters: (1) line count and spacing — the standard five-line staff, with three-line (early neumes) and four-line (medieval chant; modern guitar tablature) variants, the line count fixing how many scale steps are visible without ledger lines; (2) pitch reference — the staff encodes relative scale steps, while absolute pitch is established by a clef placed at its start that fixes a named note to a specific line or space (G-, F-, and C-clefs); (3) system layout — staves grouped into horizontal systems on a page and stacked vertically into multi-part scores (the two-staff grand staff for piano; the four-staff choral score); (4) extension — notes beyond the staff's range sit on ledger lines, short continuations of the staff. Persistence mechanism: standardized since the medieval monastic reform of notation (Guido's four-line staff; the five-line staff by the fourteenth century), reproduced through engraving, typesetting, and digital notation software, and maintained through music pedagogy — the staff persists as the frame within which clefs, noteheads, bar lines, and dynamic markings operate. It is distinguished from musical-notation (the whole symbolic framework), clef (the glyph that keys the staff's pitch reference), and bar (the unit of time delimited on the staff): the staff is the frame, the clef its key, the bar its time, notation the system that contains all three. payload.body: A note is the atomic notational unit of written music: a glyph — a notehead placed on a line or space of a staff, optionally with a stem and flags or beams — that fixes one pitch and one duration. It is distinguished from pitch (the acoustic property the note denotes), staff (the frame on which it is placed), clef (the key that fixes its pitch reference), and bar (the unit of time that groups it). payload.body: A barline is the vertical line drawn across a staff that delimits bars (measures): a boundary mark separating one unit of musical time from the next, by which the beat structure set by the time signature is grouped into the recurring segments the eye can navigate. Parameters: (1) position — drawn perpendicular to the staff lines at a bar boundary, spanning the full height of the staff, and in multi-staff systems the same line links every staff of the system so the boundary is visible across parts; (2) kinds — the single thin line at an ordinary bar boundary; the heavier single line closing a section; and the thick-thin final barline closing a piece or a major section; (3) function — the barline is the mark that makes the bar visible: the bar is the unit of musical time the barline delimits, and the two are distinct carvings (the board's accepted definition of bar names the barline as its visual marker). Persistence mechanism: engraved, printed, or digitally rendered as a mark of the score; sustained through the shared conventions of Western staff notation, the engraving and typesetting traditions that place the mark at every boundary, and pedagogy that transmits the convention from score to score and player to player. [formal: linea barica | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.scope: A human-made element of Western musical notation: a glyph (an arc enclosing a dot) placed over a note, chord, or rest that suspends its rhythm, built to persist as part of the standard notation system through shared performance convention, engraving and typesetting practice, and teaching.

payload.body: A fermata is the notational glyph — a small arc or squared bracket enclosing a dot, placed above (or less often below) a notehead, chord, or rest — that suspends the rhythm at that point: the performer holds the sounding note or the silence beyond its notated value, at discretion, before the flow proceeds. Parameters: (1) form — the standard mark is a curve enclosing a point; textual spellings ('fermata', 'hold', 'al fermata') name the same instruction, and the mark is distinct from the segno, a repeat and navigation marker; (2) application — the mark attaches to a single note, chord, or rest, not to a passage, and is distinct from the tenuto, which sustains a value without extending it; (3) duration — unlike a rest, which fixes a definite length of silence, the fermata fixes no value at all: the hold's length is determined by the performer, the genre's tradition, and the surrounding context, which is precisely why the mark is a suspension rather than a duration; (4) function — the fermata suspends the beat flow at its point of application, producing the rhetorical pause that the score marks but does not measure. Persistence mechanism: standardized in Western staff notation as an engraved, printed, or digitally rendered glyph; sustained through performance convention, the engraving and typesetting traditions that place the mark where the composer writes it, and pedagogy that transmits the instruction from score to score and player to player. [formal: fermata | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.scope: A human-made mathematical function mapping real numbers to positive reals, defined as the power of the base e, built to persist as the canonical growth function of analysis and computation through mathematical formalism, pedagogy, and numerical libraries.

payload.body: The exponential function is a human-made mathematical function that assigns to each real number x the value obtained by raising the base e (Euler's number, ≈ 2.718281828) to the power x, written exp(x) or e^x. Parameters: (1) base — fixed at e, the unique number for which the function's rate of growth equals its value at every point; (2) domain — all real numbers (extendable to the complex plane in the complex exponential); (3) codomain — the positive reals, never zero or negative; (4) equivalent defining representations — the power series ∑_{n=0}^∞ x^n/n!, the unique solution of the differential equation f'(x) = f(x) with f(0) = 1, and the inverse of the natural logarithm, exp(x) = y ⇔ ln(y) = x; (5) fundamental identities — exp(x + y) = exp(x)·exp(y) and exp(0) = 1, which make it the unique homomorphism from (R, +) to (R+, ×). Persistence mechanism: formalized in 18th-century analysis (Euler introduced the notation e^x and the constant e), carried through the calculus curriculum and mathematical analysis textbooks, and implemented in the numerical libraries of every computing environment as exp() under IEEE-754 practice. [formal: functio exponentialis | substrate: mind | horizon: generations | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

The logarithm existed and fed into the exponential's formulation; the arrow points from the later object to the earlier source.

payload.body: Priming is the human-made conceptual framework describing the unconscious, non-deliberate activation of specific associations in memory that subsequently influences perception, cognition, and behavior. PARAMETERS: (1) the prime — an explicitly or implicitly presented stimulus (word, image, concept, context) that activates an association, (2) the target — the subsequent stimulus or task affected by the activated association, (3) the interval — the time between prime and target, typically milliseconds to minutes, (4) the match — the semantic, perceptual, or feature overlap between prime and target. PERSISTENCE: priming persists through repeated demonstration in experimental paradigms — semantic priming (cats activates dog), repetition priming (prior exposure speeds recognition), affective priming (prior emotion affects judgment), and procedural priming (prior action facilitates execution). The concept persists as a theoretical construct in cognitive psychology and neuroscience, operationalized through reaction-time measures, priming thresholds, and neural activation patterns. It is distinguished from memory retrieval (conscious recall), learning (stable performance change), and expectation (deliberate prediction). [formal: priming | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: The Bartlett window is the triangular window function that tapers a finite data segment linearly from a peak of 1 at the centre to 0 at both ends: w(n) = 1 - |2n - (N - 1)|/(N - 1), n = 0..N-1. PARAMETERS: (1) length N — the number of samples the triangle spans; (2) symmetry form — the symmetric form (even about the midpoint (N-1)/2, w(0) = 0), used in filter design, versus the periodic form (w(0) = 1, meant to tile across adjacent segments), used in spectral estimation; (3) the resulting spectral shape — a sinc-squared main lobe twice as wide as a same-length rectangular window, a first side lobe near -26 dB, and a 1/f^4 falloff. PERSISTENCE: the formula persists as a named standard — the discrete autocorrelation of a rectangular pulse, equivalently the convolution of two rectangular windows — in signal-processing textbooks, in DSP and codec toolkits where the triangular taper recurs in resampling and filtering routines, and in spectral-estimation practice as the simplest non-rectangular taper and the reference case against which smoother windows (Hamming, Hann, Blackman) are compared. It is distinguished from the Bartlett method (periodogram averaging, which applies a RECTANGULAR smoothing window per segment) — a same-named, same-origin construct that is not this window — and from the generic triangle-shaped taper of which it is the canonical named instance in DSP usage. [formal: bartlett-window | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.scope: A human-made window function — the three-term cosine-sum taper with a first side lobe near -58 dB, persisting as a standard formula in signal-processing textbooks and DSP toolkits where side-lobe suppression outweighs main-lobe broadening.

payload.body: The Blackman window is the three-term cosine-sum window function: w(n) = 0.42 - 0.5*cos(2*pi*n/(N-1)) + 0.08*cos(4*pi*n/(N-1)), n = 0..N-1, its coefficients chosen so the first three side lobes cancel. PARAMETERS: (1) length N — the number of samples the window spans; (2) form — the symmetric form (w(0) = w(N-1) = 0, even about (N-1)/2) used in filter design, versus the periodic form w(n) = 0.42 - 0.5*cos(2*pi*n/N) + 0.08*cos(4*pi*n/N) used in spectral estimation, where the window tiles across adjacent segments; (3) spectral shape — a main lobe four bins wide (double the same-length rectangular window), a first side lobe near -58 dB, and a 1/f^6 falloff, the lowest first side lobe among the standard two- and three-term cosine windows. PERSISTENCE: the formula persists as a named standard in signal-processing textbooks (the classic three-term cosine-sum design, attributed to Ralph Blackman), in DSP and audio toolkits where it is the default choice when side-lobe suppression outweighs main-lobe broadening, and in spectral-estimation practice as the middle step of the cosine-window ladder between Hann (near -31 dB first side lobe) and the four-term Blackman-Harris variant (near -92 dB). It is distinguished from the Blackman-Harris window — a different named standard sharing the prefix, with a fourth cosine term — and from the generic cosine-sum taper family of which it is the canonical three-term member. [formal: blackman-window | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.name: equal-temperament
payload.scope: A human-made tuning system — the convention dividing the octave into twelve equal semitones — built to persist as the dominant interval framework of Western music through instrument manufacture, international pitch standards, and notation.

payload.name: equal-temperament
payload.scope: A human-made tuning system — the convention dividing the octave into twelve equal semitones — built to persist as the dominant interval framework of Western music through instrument manufacture, international pitch standards, and notation.

payload.body: Equal temperament is a human-made tuning system in which the octave is divided into twelve equal steps, each step (the chromatic semitone) carrying a frequency ratio of 2^(1/12) ≈ 1.059463, exactly 100 cents. Parameters: (1) frame — the octave, the 2:1 frequency ratio being divided; (2) division — twelve equal steps, no one larger or smaller than the rest; (3) step ratio — 2^(1/12) per step, so that twelve steps compound to exactly 2:1; (4) interval compromise — the octave and tritone remain exact while the perfect fifth (700 vs ~702 cents) and the major and minor thirds are slightly tempered, the price that makes transposition and modulation to all twelve keys possible without retuning. Persistence mechanism: standardized in the physical manufacture of keyboard and fretted instruments (twelve frets per octave, the piano's twelve-key octave), in the international concert-pitch framework (A4 = 440 Hz on 100-cent steps), in staff notation convention (the chromatic staff with accidentals), and in audio software tuning; reproduced through manufacturing, pedagogy, and repertoire. [formal: temperamentum aequale | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.body: Semitone is the smallest named interval of Western chromatic music — the distance between two adjacent pitch classes, named in two qualities: the diatonic semitone (a minor second, e.g. E–F or B–C, spanning two adjacent letter names) and the chromatic semitone (an augmented unison or diminished second, e.g. C–C#, spanning one letter name). Parameters: (1) quality — diatonic or chromatic, fixed by the letter names of the endpoints; (2) size in cents — exactly 100 in equal temperament, roughly 112 (diatonic, 16:15) and roughly 90 (chromatic, 256:243) in just intonation; (3) notation — written as a one-step staff movement with an accidental, or as two adjacent staff positions. Persistence mechanism: maintained through interval nomenclature and scale theory, the physical layout of keyboard and fretted instruments (adjacent white and black keys, one fret per semitone), the accidental system of staff notation, and pedagogy; the name survives in standard interval naming and in the cent scale. [formal: semitonum | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

Equal temperament's accepted definition carves a human-made tuning system in which the octave is divided into twelve equal steps, each step (the chromatic semitone) carrying ratio 2^(1/12). Removing the concept of semitone as a named interval does not stop the system from operating — instruments still produce twelve equal divisions of the octave, the ratio 2^(1/12) remains operative, and transposition remains possible. The semitone is a naming artifact of the system, not an operational prerequisite. The accepted DEPENDS_ON edge to octave correctly captures the constitutive frame; the semitone dependency is a generic appeal to language rather than a removal test that stops operation. Therefore the edge should be struck.

payload.name: language-variety
payload.scope: A human-made analytical genus of sociolinguistics: the category of systematic, rule-governed linguistic forms that a speech community distinguishes, built to persist as the discipline's instrument for sorting dialects, idiolects, and their kin by the population or situation that characterizes them.

payload.name: language-variety
payload.scope: A human-made analytical genus of sociolinguistics: the category of systematic, rule-governed linguistic forms that a speech community distinguishes, built to persist as the discipline's instrument for sorting dialects, idiolects, and their kin by the population or situation that characterizes them.

payload.body: Language-variety is the analytical genus under which a speech community's linguistic forms are sorted: a form counts as a variety when it is (1) internally rule-governed — stable, systematic conventions of phonology, lexicon, and grammar rather than noise or error; (2) distinguished from other forms of the same language by the population or situation that characterizes it — a region, a social group, a single individual, or a context of use; and (3) nameable and recognizable in the community's analytic practice, identifiable by speakers and analysts alike. Its parameters are the level of description at which the variety is carved — group-level (dialect, sociolect, regional form), individual-level (idiolect), situational-level (register) — and the social index that marks it. Persistence mechanism: the genus persists as an instrument of the discipline — codified in sociolinguistic research and teaching, applied whenever a community's speech is documented, contrasted, or socially indexed, and re-applied to new data without being altered by it. Where the territory is a continuum of variation, the map draws the cells: it is the made scaffold that makes dialect and idiolect comparable units of one science, rather than siblings defined only against each other. [formal: varietas linguarum | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.50]

payload.body: Signal-processing is a human-made framework of methods for analyzing and transforming signals across any representation domain — time, frequency, spatial, or other domains. It operates by applying mathematical operations (filtering, modulation, transformation, compression) to signal representations to extract information, modify characteristics, or prepare signals for further use. Parameters: (1) signal type (analog, digital, discrete-time, discrete-frequency), (2) representation domain (time, frequency, cepstral, wavelet), (3) processing objective (extraction, modification, compression, synthesis). Persistence mechanism: encoded in signal processing theory (textbooks, academic curricula), implemented in software libraries (MATLAB, Python SciPy/NumPy, GNU Radio), deployed in hardware (DSP chips, FPGA, ASIC), and sustained through the practice of communications engineering, audio engineering, and data science communities. payload.body: A function is a human-made mathematical structure that assigns to each element of a first set (the domain) exactly one element of a second set (the codomain), written f: A → B with f(x) = y. Parameters: (1) domain — the set of inputs over which the function is defined; (2) codomain — the set of permitted outputs, of which the range (image) actually reached by the domain may be a proper subset; (3) assignment rule — the correspondence selecting the output for each input, given by formula, table, graph, algorithm, or verbal description; (4) uniqueness — no input is assigned to two distinct outputs, which is exactly what separates a function from a general relation. Persistence mechanism: fixed by set-theoretic formalism (a function is a set of ordered pairs with the uniqueness property), carried by algebraic and calculus notation (f(x), the arrow, composition f∘g), taught as the central object of mathematical modeling in the school and university curriculum, and instantiated as the function construct of every programming language. [formal: functio | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.body: A key is a human-made musical framework: an organized set of pitches whose members bear functional roles defined by their relation to a central pitch, the tonic. Parameters: (1) tonic — the central pitch class of the framework, the point of departure and resolution, the pitch at which phrases and progressions come to rest; (2) quality — the intervallic pattern above the tonic fixing the major or minor mode (the major whole-step/half-step pattern, or its minor variants), giving the key its characteristic color; (3) diatonic pitch set — the scale tones organized into a functional hierarchy (tonic, dominant, subdominant, and secondary functions) that determines which chords and melodic motions sound stable or unstable; (4) transposition invariance — the framework is relocatable to any of the twelve pitch classes, so the twelve keys of a given quality are the same structure shifted in pitch. Persistence mechanism: key signatures in staff notation (the sharps or flats that name the framework), the circle of fifths as the structural map of key relations, harmony pedagogy teaching functional progression and cadence in terms of the key, the practice of composition, analysis, and performance naming works by their key ('in D minor'), and the equal-tempered instrument layout reproducing the twelve keys as playable sets. [formal: clavis | substrate: mind | horizon: centuries | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

A bar is a unit WITHIN that system — the measure delimited by barlines — not a kind of it. The defensible relation is musical-notation CONTAINS bar.
